title: Unify the tenant-scope trio across fourteen services behind one tested implementation
goal: Eleven system services and three auth services each implement the same three-part helper: take the tenant from the gin context, build a scoped *gorm.DB, and resolve the owner tenant id. The copies are structurally identical but they are also the multi-tenant isolation hot path, which is why the audit put them in the last batch. This wave first pins the current behaviour with a before-snapshot test and a two-tenant end-to-end case that does not exist yet, then replaces the copies with one implementation in pkg/tenant, then proves that no query lost its tenant predicate. If the two-tenant case cannot be constructed, the wave stops rather than proceeds on static reasoning.
findings: RC-012 (P1): the tenant-scope trio is duplicated at role_service.go:27-50, post_service.go:29-50, dept_service.go:31-53, user_service.go:46-74 (including a double wrapper at :58 and :63), dict_service.go:58-82, setting_service.go:59-89, permission_service.go:67-83, dashboard_service.go:54 and :349-352, login_service.go:51-58, security_service.go:128, session_service.go:79.
RC-027 (P1): the auth module carries the same duplication plus its own pagination at login_service.go:273,286, session_service.go:460,504 and security_service.go:208-229,722.

Open gap: the audit found no existing two-tenant isolation smoke in the repository. The nearest evidence is the historical isolation remediation packet and its one-off acceptance scripts, which are not part of the default test run.

in: Add one tenant-scope helper in backend/pkg/tenant and prove it reproduces the current semantics for compat, multi and nil contexts
Pin the current behaviour first: a table-driven test asserting the scoped DB for tenant 0, a non-zero tenant and a missing context
Construct a two-tenant end-to-end case that proves a subject in tenant A cannot list, read, update or delete tenant B's row for every affected module
Replace the eleven system-service and three auth-service copies with the shared helper
Remove the user_service.go double wrapper as part of the replacement
Leave every other query predicate untouched
out: Changing tenant resolution rules, compat behaviour, or the platform-global tenant id
Changing the fail-closed behaviour for a missing tenant context
Changing any route, permission code, menu or error message
Introducing request-scoped caching or a new middleware

implementationNotes: Stop condition: if the two-tenant end-to-end case cannot be built in this environment, do not proceed on static analysis alone. Record the blocker and close the wave as blocked.
Write the before-snapshot first. It must fail if a predicate is dropped, otherwise it proves nothing.

The three contexts are genuinely different: nil means an internal caller that intentionally wants the unfiltered service, compat means tenant_id = 0, multi means a non-zero tenant. The helper must preserve all three; collapsing compat into nil was the exact defect fixed in the 2026-10-24 packet.
Preserve fail-closed: a missing or malformed tenant context must not fall back to an unfiltered query.
Do not change what each query filters on beyond the tenant predicate. Data-scope predicates and dept predicates stay where they are.
Replace one service per commit and run that service's tests plus the two-tenant case before moving on.

executionRoles.implementerPosture: Behaviour pin first, then one service per commit, then the two-tenant case after each conversion.
reviewerPosture: Check every converted query still carries its tenant predicate or an explicit platform-scope justification.
Check compat, multi and nil contexts each resolve exactly as before.
Check fail-closed is preserved for a missing context.
Check no other predicate changed in the same commit.
Check the two-tenant case actually exercises both directions.

runtimeEvidence: two-tenant case: tenant A lists, reads, updates and deletes its own rows; the same operations against tenant B's ids return empty, 404 or 403 with no existence leak
compat-mode case: a tenant_id = 0 record remains visible and editable and a tenant row does not appear
before/after scoped-DB snapshot for one query per converted service

humanGates: Approve proceeding without a pre-existing two-tenant smoke, or provide the environment and credentials to build one.
Approve the wave at all: it changes the multi-tenant isolation hot path for a net saving of roughly 250-400 lines.
completionChecklist: One tenant-scope implementation exists with a before-snapshot test
Fourteen services call the shared helper and no copy remains
Two-tenant case passes in both directions
Compat and nil contexts behave exactly as before
No query lost its predicate and no other predicate changed
